answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through subterranean acoustic attestation. To authenticate, an agent transmits an acoustic signal into a karst aquifer, capturing the echo scattered by a reference pearl inside a monitoring borehole. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of securing scarce land parcels and maintaining dedicated downhole hardware per identity. However, seasonal water table fluctuations alter the acoustic signature, occasionally triggering false rejections.
